newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope condemns school massacre in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: Pope condemns school massacre in Burundi.

text.p: Pope John Paul, expressing outrage at a massacre of students and teachers in Burundi, has urged the African country to seek peace through dialogue and forgiveness, Vatican Radio said on Friday.

It said the Pope made his appeal in a telegram sent to the Roman Catholic bishop in the southern Bururi region, where suspected Hutu rebels killed 38 students and seven Catholic lay teachers at a school in the village of Buta on Tuesday.
Another 40 students were wounded in the attack, according to reports from Burundi-based U.N. human rights observers.
"The Pope strongly condemns such barbaric acts and again repeats that nothing good can come of violence," the radio quoted the telegram as saying.

"He also asks all members of the village to abandon all feelings of hate and revenge, and to finally seek the only way leading to a future for the country -- the way of dialogue, forgiveness and understanding," it added.
More than 150,000 people, mostly civilians, have been killed in massacres and civil war in Burundi since Tutsi troops killed Burundi's first Hutu president in 1993.
The United Nations said on Friday that tens of people were dying daily in new outbreaks of violence in southern Burundi, where a mainly Tutsi army is fighting majority Hutu rebels.
